ground_truth.mechanism: recommendation/recommendation_server.py get_product_list (lines 66-98 at tag 3.0.0): with the flag on, each call is a cache miss with probability 0.5; a miss calls ProductCatalogService/ListProducts, appends the 10 catalog ids to the module-global cached_ids and then appends a quarter of the list to itself, so the list grows by about 1.25x per miss and is never deduplicated or trimmed. demo.product.count on the get_product_list span is len(cached_ids): 10 on every baseline span, 12 after the first miss, and 3,393,387 after 21 minutes live on 2026-09-27. Span duration follows the list size (baseline median about 5 ms; 143-159 ms at 2.7-3.4 million). No span sets ERROR status. frontend's RecommendationService/ListRecommendations client span and GET /api/recommendations slow down only once the count passes about 1 million; those are cascading symptoms.

notes: Evidence: live flag window 2026-09-27 04:57:26Z to 05:18:47Z (21.4 min) on quay.io/jaegertracing/jaeger:2.20.0, fresh recommendation process (no cache activity before the flip). Baseline: demo.product.count = 10 on all 287 get_product_list spans in the hour before the flip and on all 8 after the restore; get_product_list median about 5 ms, max 36.6 ms; zero ERROR spans in recommendation traces. Under the fault the count passed 100 at about 3 min, 1,000 at about 5 min, 10,000 at about 8 min, 100,000 at about 12 min and 1,000,000 at about 19 min (50 misses in 101 calls). signal_regex is magnitude, not presence: three or more digits (>= 100) is 10x the only baseline value ever seen, and it is reached after 5 misses, well inside bench.py's 8 minute trace poll. The regex matches all three renderings: the MCP get_span_details form ("demo.product.count":N), the Jaeger API file form and bench.py's json.dumps form ("key": "demo.product.count", "type": "int64", "value": N); demo.product.filtered.count never matches. deterministic is bucketed: the direction is certain but the rate is stochastic (a fair coin per call times bursty load-generator traffic, about 48 recommendation traces per 10 min), so what a trial sees depends on how long the fault has run. The trap: there is no error to find. An error-first agent (search_traces with_errors) finds only pre-existing frontend-proxy 504s on POST /api/checkout (15.7 s upstream timeouts, present at baseline and under the fault) and occasional ad errors; recommendation returns zero error traces. The signal is a span attribute that only get_span_details shows, and the frontend slowdown the prompt describes is only measurable once the count is past about 1 million. demo.recommendation.cache_hit appears only under the fault (absent at baseline once the collector strips demo.feature_flag.recommendation_cache); it is a mechanism hint, not a flag name, and fixture_leak passes on the evidence trace. Fixture caveats: cached_ids lives in the recommendation process and is NOT cleared by restoring the flag; the next flip starts from the old list (3,393,387 after this window, recommendation memory 65 to 98 MiB of a 500 MiB limit), and continued growth ends in an OOM restart that resets the count to 12 (seen 2026-09-10). A batch should start from a freshly started recommendation container. Operation: get_product_list is the span that carries the growing count; the recommendation server span oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations wraps it and is accepted, as PlaceOrder is for paymentUnreachable. 2026-09-27: signal raised to a count of one million or more and signal_wait_s 1800, so trials start only once the fault is user-visible (frontend recommendation latency rises past a count of about 1M, measured the same day).
